sections.html:
Bloomington is the McLean County seat in central Illinois, covering 27.24 square miles. The count was 78,680 in 2020 and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 78,804. Median value of owner homes is $203,300, 61.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, median gross rent is $1,050 and the average commute is 16.8 minutes.

Local employers such as State Farm and Illinois State University in neighboring Normal keep a steady pool of buyers. Shoppers compare Bloomington and Normal houses side by side, so look at recent sales in both before you set a price.

Two public districts cover the city. Bloomington Public Schools District 87 serves the interior with Bloomington High School, Bloomington Junior High and six elementary schools. Growth pushed the city well into McLean County Unit District No. 5, which runs Normal Community High School and Normal Community West High School. A small part of the city lies in Olympia Community Unit School District 16, and Central Catholic High School is a private option.

The district can change from one block to the next, so confirm it for your address before you write the listing description. A buyer with children will ask first, and a wrong answer can sink a showing.

Anyone who owns residential rental property inside the city limits must register it with the city and hold a Certificate of Inspection before renting or leasing a unit. If you are selling a rental, the rules shape what a buyer inherits.

Bloomington rental program costs
Fee or taxAmount
Registration, per building$65
Added per rental unit, buildings of three or more units$5
Follow-up inspection$100
Missed inspection$75
Short Term Rental Tax, stays under 30 days6.0 percent
  • The first inspection is included in the registration fee, and each owned condo needs its own registration.
  • Registrations run until December 31 each year and cannot be transferred to new owners, so a buyer must register on their own.
  • Owners get at least 15 days' notice of an inspection, and inspectors enforce the International Property Maintenance Code, the Fire Code and other city ordinances.
  • A building rated fair may be required to post a $5,000 letter of credit or pledged account until it receives a passing rating.
  • Violations not fixed by the reinspection date lead to a court appearance and possible court costs.

Short-term rental tax is due by the 25th of the following month, with a 5 percent penalty for late payments, and those operators must also register the unit annually in the rental program. Settle any unpaid tax or inspection issue before closing.

A cash buyer will often take on a tenant-occupied or violation-heavy property as-is, which can avoid a repair-and-reinspect cycle. The city's rules still follow whoever owns the building, so agree in writing on who handles reinspection after closing.

Fees or court matters tied to your ownership are yours to clear first. Ask the city for a current list of open items on the address, and keep inspection reports and any passing rating with your sale papers.

The McLean County Clerk's office handles recording at 115 E. Washington Street, Bloomington. Its Predictable Recording Fee Schedule, effective July 1, 2023, sets a standard document at $61.00. Documents exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee, such as government filings and powers of attorney, are $41.00, and a non-standard document is $75.00.

A document counts as non-standard if it uses legal- or ledger-size paper or has six or more PIN or related-document references. Recorded documents must be originals or certified copies. Certified copies cost $18.00 and additional copies $1.00 per page. The recording phone is (309) 888-5170.

The state transfer declaration and any transfer tax are separate from the recording fee. Your title company collects them at closing, so ask for an itemized settlement statement and compare it with the schedule above.

You have 30 days from the publication date shown for your township to file an assessment complaint with the Board of Review, and a late complaint will not be heard. The county posts each township's publication and deadline dates in a table, and the Board of Review office is at (309) 888-5132. For 2026 the equalization factors were 1.0534 for the Bloomington township and 1.0385 for the City of Bloomington township.

The county uses Form PTAX-230 for non-farm complaints. The assessment is based on the past three years' market value before January 1 of the assessment year, with a multiplier applied to bring the statutory assessment to 33.33 percent. The City of Bloomington Township Assessor keeps property record cards and a lookup tool you can use to compare your house with neighbors.

Ask the County Treasurer for installment dates and a payoff figure before closing. The proration on the settlement statement depends on which installments are paid. If you plan to appeal, file inside the 30-day window each year and keep the decision with your records, since a buyer may ask what happened.

A cash sale skips a buyer's loan approval but still runs through the same recording and tax steps. Here is the usual order.

  • Gather the deed, the latest tax bill, any rental registration and inspection reports, and records of repairs.
  • Confirm which school district and which township assessor cover your address.
  • Ask the County Treasurer for a payoff figure and installment dates.
  • Give your title company the buyer's details early so the settlement statement is ready before the closing date.
  • At closing, check the itemized statement for the recording fee, the state declaration and any transfer tax, then sign the deed for recording at the County Clerk's office.

If the house is vacant or occupied by tenants, say so up front. Buyers who purchase as-is price in the condition, and a clear list of what you know saves time on both sides. Tenants who rent month to month or hold a lease can affect the closing date, so bring a copy of the lease to your first conversation with a buyer.

faqs.q: Can a new owner use the previous owner's Bloomington rental registration?
faqs.a: No. Registrations cannot be transferred to new owners. A buyer who plans to rent must register the building, pay the registration fee and pass inspection.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in McLean County?
faqs.a: The schedule effective July 1, 2023 sets $61.00 for a standard document and $75.00 for a non-standard one. Fees can change, so confirm with the County Clerk before sending payment.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a McLean County assessment?
faqs.a: Taxpayers have 30 days from the publication date shown for their township, and late complaints are not heard. Check the county's table each year for your township's dates.

faqs.q: Is the short-term rental tax applied to every Bloomington short-term stay?
faqs.a: The city applies a 6.0 percent tax to rentals of less than 30 days. Operators who use a listing site must still register each property and file monthly certification forms.

faqs.q: Does a cash sale remove the need to fix rental violations in Bloomington?
faqs.a: The city's rules still apply to whoever owns the building, but a cash buyer may agree to buy as-is and handle repairs and reinspection after closing. Settle fees or court matters tied to your ownership first, and get any sale terms in writing.
